acts: If detained: ask why, tell family, get a lawyer · NALSA 15100
Check the date and the source first

cases.name: Umar Khalid
cases.status: Delhi High Court rejected his bail for the third time on 30 Sep 2026; trial not begun. Prosecution said he cannot seek bail again before Jan 2027

cases.name: Sharjeel Imam
cases.status: Bail rejected by Delhi High Court 30 Sep 2026. A 7-day interim bail ended 10 Oct; a court found a media-contact breach but did not cancel it. Police called it misuse of liberty

cases.name: Srishti Gupta
cases.status: No bail in 2 of 11 cases. Her bail order notes she was not at the site of the violence; police chargesheet calls her a key conspirator

cases.name: Satyam Verma
cases.law: NSA (order 12 May 2026) plus Noida protest FIRs
cases.status: Journalist still held under NSA despite bail in one case on 15 Sep. Allahabad High Court reserved its verdict on his NSA challenge on 8 Oct; state's arguments not reported

cases.name: Pranab Doley
cases.status: Held under NSA after getting bail. Gauhati High Court reserved its verdict on his challenge on 14 Oct. Govt cites public order; Assam Police did not answer press questions

cases.name: Siang dam protesters (4)
cases.status: Four Geku villagers still held. After the 23 Oct arson in Pasighat, police say 69 people were arrested under the same law. CM has offered talks

cases.name: Dawit Isaak
cases.status: Journalist held incommunicado 25 years; whereabouts and health unknown. Eritrea's president said in 2009 there would be no trial and no release

cases.name: Abdulhadi Al-Khawaja
cases.status: Human rights defender in Jau Prison; rights groups urged France's president to press for his release before his 20 Oct visit. No Bahraini government response reported

cases.name: Osman Kavala
cases.status: Istanbul court refused release and retrial (13 Oct) despite a European Court of Human Rights ruling; government says courts are independent and the case is not political

cases.name: Jimmy Lai
cases.status: Serving 20 years, aged 78. UK urged his release (22 Oct); Hong Kong rejected this, saying he was not tried for his political views

cases.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
cases.status: Under house arrest in Naypyidaw; spoke to her son by phone on 22 Oct, the first time in five years. Government rejects calls for release

cases.name: Imran Aliyev
cases.law: Smuggling, money laundering, tax evasion, forgery charges
cases.status: Meclis.info founder; prosecutors sought 12 years (20 Oct), verdict expected 3 Nov. Authorities say outlets broke foreign-grant rules

cases.name: Dr Hussam Abu Safiya
cases.law: Unlawful Combatants Law; no charge, no trial
cases.status: Hospital director; lawyer reports abuse in custody. Israel alleges Hamas links, which family and lawyers deny

cases.name: Detainees held by the RSF
cases.countcap: held in El Geneina, doctors say
cases.status: Amnesty reports torture, forced labour and ransom-for-release in El Fasher; doctors report food shortages and deaths in El Geneina. RSF did not respond

cases.name: Najmeh Amini
cases.law: Death sentence for blasphemy; 12.5 years on security charges
cases.status: 23-year-old student held in Mashhad Central Prison, sentenced to death over social media posts. No official statement reported
src: Center for Human Rights in Iran

cases.name: Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha
cases.law: Anti-Terrorism Act; earlier 17 years under electronic crimes law (PECA)
cases.status: Human rights lawyers sentenced to 10 years on 29 Oct after trial inside Adiala prison. Law minister says the judiciary is independent

cases.name: Artin Ghazanfari
cases.law: 26 years incl. 'media activities' under espionage-penalties law
cases.status: Baha'i photojournalist with heart failure; judge reportedly refused hospital transfer. Sentence told to him on 26 Oct. Iran did not respond to CPJ

cases.name: Mountaga Tall
cases.status: Lawyer and junta critic abducted in Bamako; his son also vanished on 16 May. Authorities have not acknowledged holding either

items.headline: Siang dam protesters detained in Delhi
items.text: Delhi Police detained protesters, including activist Katon Moyong, outside Arunachal Bhawan on Saturday as they opposed the Siang dam. Organisers say about 40 were held and allege some were sexually assaulted; some were later released. No Delhi Police response to the allegations was reported.

items.headline: Three Kuki men killed in Noney gunfight
items.text: Three Kuki men were killed on Saturday in a gunfight between armed groups at Kekru Naga village, police said, adding that security had been stepped up. The Kuki Inpi Manipur said the dead were village volunteers and blamed Naga armed groups; police have not identified those responsible.

items.headline: Four workers die in Delhi shoe factory fire
items.text: Four workers died in a fire at a shoe factory in Mangolpuri; relatives allege they were made to work extra hours in the festive season. Police arrested two management members on Saturday and filed an FIR for culpable homicide and negligence against the owner and others.

items.headline: Playwright smeared with ink during Gandhi play
items.text: Protesters objecting to a play's portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi smeared ink on playwright Addanda Cariappa during a show in Bengaluru on Saturday. A complaint has been filed at Banashankari police station and police say investigations are on; the protesters' own complaint seeks action against Cariappa.

items.headline: Journalist's website taken offline by host
items.text: Hosting firm Hostinger suspended journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta's website on 28 October over a "Fraud/Scam" abuse report, days after a court ordered one 2019 article removed in a defamation suit. In a statement on Saturday he called it backdoor censorship; Hostinger support said suspension was "not negotiable".

items.place: Press Club of India, New Delhi
items.headline: Tribunal says July protest policing was excessive
items.text: A people's tribunal of retired civil servants, chaired by former judge Anjana Prakash, reported on Saturday that Delhi Police used disproportionate force and arbitrary mass detentions against July's exam-leak protests. It heard 25 people; Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force were invited but did not respond.

items.headline: UN chief condemns escalating Sudan drone strikes
items.text: On Saturday UN Secretary-General Guterres, through his spokesman, condemned escalating drone attacks by the parties in Sudan, after Monday's strike on Nyala's Tanqonj market killed at least 102 people. The strike has been attributed to the army. No army or RSF response was reported.

items.headline: Four Palestinians die in Gaza despite ceasefire
items.text: Hospitals said Israeli shelling of Nuseirat killed a teacher, a man died of earlier strike wounds, and two girls died after a tent fire of unclear cause in al-Mawasi. Gaza's health ministry counts 1,580 killed since the ceasefire. No Israeli military comment was reported.

items.place: Paris, Lyon and cities across France
items.headline: Police fire tear gas at French youth protests
items.text: Authorities counted 320,000 marchers on Saturday's cost-of-living and schools protests, organisers nearly half a million. Police used tear gas in Paris and Lyon and the interior ministry reported at least 290 arrests. The government says it has heard protesters and is studying cost-of-living measures.

items.headline: London police arrest 139 at Palestine Action protest
items.text: Police arrested 139 people at a protest outside the US embassy against the ban on Palestine Action, mostly for expressing support for a proscribed group, the Metropolitan Police said. Organisers Defend Our Juries call the vigils peaceful and say arrests under the ban now exceed 4,000.

items.headline: UN rights chief seeks probe into detainee death
items.text: UN rights chief Volker Türk demanded an independent investigation into the death of staffer Mohammad el Shami, held by Houthi authorities since June 2024, whose family learned of it weeks late. The UN says 71 personnel remain detained. No Houthi response was reported.

items.place: Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Frankfurt, Germany
items.headline: Gen Z protests spread across German cities
items.text: Youth-led rallies on Saturday over living costs, education cuts and conscription drew 5,000 in Berlin by police count and 10,000 by organisers, who claim 100,000–120,000 nationwide. Police used water cannon in Cologne, saying their measures targeted violent individuals, not peaceful participants.

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. After arson in Pasighat on 23 October, police say 69 people have been arrested; on 31 October Delhi Police detained protesters outside Arunachal Bhawan, who allege sexual assault.
focus.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
